 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Aliyah Boston loves playing alongside Caitlin Clark, and the Indiana Fever star made her feelings clear about her teammate in a comment on social media.
 While the Fever failed to make a deep run in the 2026 WNBA playoffs, losing to the Las Vegas Aces in the first round, there's no denying that Clark had a phenomenal season.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Clark averaged 22.3 points and a team-high 8.3 assists per game during the season, finishing third in the league in scoring and second in assists. She was the first player in WNBA history to be in the top three in both statistical categories.
 Indiana Fever guards Caitlin Clark (22) and Sophie Cunningham (8) talk on the bench.Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect
 Weeks after their 2026 postseason run ended, Clark took to social media to reflect on her campaign and expressed her relief at being able to stay healthy following an injury-riddled year. The All-Star guard had played in only 13 games in 2025 and missed the playoffs due to a groin injury and a bone bruise.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Thankful for a season of being healthy and doing what I love," Clark wrote, while sharing several photos of herself and her teammates taken during the season. "Had so much fun this year, but now it's back to work … and lots of really cool shoes still on the way."
 Boston, for her part, commented on Clark's post and shared her desire to continue playing alongside her teammate for years to come.
 "lets keep it goinggg," Boston wrote.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Clark and Boston are the Fever's cornerstones, and it's hard to see the Fever parting ways with either of them. Last season, Indiana signed Boston to a four-year, $6.3 million extension under the WNBA's new Exceptional Performance on Initial Contract (EPIC) provision.
 Clark is eligible to sign an extension under the same provision as well, and the Fever are expected to discuss a potential deal with her this offseason.
